workstreams.name: Core analysis and visualizer workflow
workstreams.basis: Imports, provider execution, stored code units, source navigation, and review workflows exist. Native Mach-O analysis stores exact-address Swift/Objective-C metadata and exposes capped, hash-checked ReIPA pseudocode alternatives; the visualizer can compare native provider outputs by canonical function identity across differing saved paths and output-language labels. Isolated pinned Glaurung and Kuna providers persist bounded native C-like pseudocode; Kuna also stores assembly, selected call/jump/reference edges, and bounded opcode sequences for same-binary lookalike context. Its v1.878 analyzer image and end-to-end worker have been exercised against a system ELF binary. A read-only Ghidra p-code emulator now persists bounded, confidence-labeled control-flow-flattening transitions and exposes them as visualizer navigation evidence; representative fixture coverage and provider comparison remain open.

workstreams.name: Database-grounded project memory and provenance
workstreams.basis: Project-scoped observations, symbols, relationships, drafts, and review records ground AI context. Common native virtual-address spellings now canonicalize across Ghidra, Glaurung, and Oxidizer for same-artifact function identity; bounded same-binary, completed-run lookups bring accepted cross-provider names into rewrite, explanation, and MCP dossier contexts for selected units with canonical-key or normalized native-identity matches, exact input-hash checks, and review-receipt verification. Legacy native address aliases remain a fallback and are labeled separately because they can denote thunks. MCP provider outputs also require exact input and saved-output hashes; accepted project-memory lookup is bounded to 100 candidate provider observations and reports possible truncation. Exact-address ReIPA pseudocode alternatives for matched Swift/Objective-C methods enter rewrite context and MCP dossiers only after same-run provenance checks. Ghidra functions persist bounded basic-block/edge/entry/exit metrics and a bounded basic-block graph for the visualizer. Control-flow-flattening recovery now persists in function observation attributes and is available to the visualizer, rewrite/explanation, and MCP dossier as confidence-labeled structural evidence; it does not establish identity or behavior. Broader identity coverage and fixture validation remain open.

workstreams.name: Major-language and format decompilation fluency
workstreams.basis: Several useful Java, .NET, Android, Python, WebAssembly, and native paths exist, and matched arm64 Mach-O methods can now show early ReIPA C-like pseudocode beside Ghidra output; optional Glaurung and Kuna providers add bounded native C-like pseudocode, with Kuna also saving assembly and selected graph edges. Kuna's analyzer has built and completed an end-to-end system-ELF smoke run, but both native alternates still need representative fixture comparison and fidelity validation. Many languages remain navigation-only, early, or represented by generic pseudocode.

workstreams.name: Maintainable editing, review, and export
workstreams.basis: Hash-bound drafts, review receipts, syntax-aware edits for selected languages, and reproducible export exist; language breadth and project-level edits remain limited.

workstreams.name: Fixture-backed validation and fidelity evidence
workstreams.basis: Provider smoke checks and structural validators exist, but broad versioned clean, optimized, stripped, and obfuscated fixture comparisons are still missing.
